tasks.title: Wrap the central-widget toolbar in a horizontal QScrollArea in place (D19 Phase 1)
tasks.description: In ui/main_window.py, wrap the existing toolbar QWidget in a QScrollArea (no frame, setWidgetResizable(False), horizontal ScrollBarAsNeeded, vertical ScrollBarAlwaysOff, fixed height 36px) and add it to the central QVBoxLayout in the toolbar's place, so the toolbar's ~1716px minimumSizeHint no longer pins the central widget while the toolbar stays inside the central widget as a single ~36px row. Give the toolbar and wrapper stable objectNames ('MainToolbar' / 'ToolbarScroll') and keep conn_badge and the trailing stretch inside the scroll region; do not touch ui/dock_layout.py, _chart_area_width, _apply_dock_widths or the cap constants. Ship tests/test_toolbar_scroll_d19.py with the wrapper-specific AC-D19.4/AC-D19.5 assertions.
acceptance_criteria: AC-D19.4(i): Given the toolbar is visible, Then the toolbar remains a descendant of centralWidget() as a single ~36px row (not moved to a QMainWindow toolbar area and no addToolBar call), and centralWidget().minimumSizeHint().width() <= CHART_MIN_WIDTH + WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH + RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH (750px), i.e. the toolbar no longer dominates that minimum.

AC-D19.4(ii): Given the toolbar is visible, Then every toolbar control remains reachable/usable — directly at a wide window and via the horizontal scroll/elide affordance at the narrowest window in which the dock minima plus chart minimum are feasible; the toolbar keeps its full natural width inside the scroll content so the horizontal scroll range is > 0 at a narrow width.

AC-D19.5: Given the toolbar is visible, When the window is resized down toward the feasible minimum, Then centralWidget().width() decreases accordingly and does not remain at the toolbar's ~1716px minimum.

Structural/mechanism: Given the wrapped toolbar, Then the wrapper is a QScrollArea with frameShape NoFrame, setWidgetResizable(False), horizontal ScrollBarPolicy ScrollBarAsNeeded, vertical ScrollBarPolicy ScrollBarAlwaysOff and a fixed height of 36px; the toolbar carries objectName 'MainToolbar', the wrapper 'ToolbarScroll', and conn_badge and the trailing stretch stay inside the scroll region (FI-D19-2); the toolbar's control set and signal wiring are unchanged.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D19.4(i): Given the toolbar is visible, Then the toolbar remains a descendant of centralWidget() as a single ~36px row (not moved to a QMainWindow toolbar area and no addToolBar call), and centralWidget().minimumSizeHint().width() <= CHART_MIN_WIDTH + WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH + RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH (750px), i.e. the toolbar no longer dominates that minimum.
tests.description: Construct an offscreen MainWindow with IBApiClient.connect monkeypatched, show it, and assert centralWidget().minimumSizeHint().width() <= 750; assert the QWidget with objectName 'MainToolbar' is a descendant of centralWidget(); assert centralWidget().layout().itemAt(0).widget() is the QScrollArea wrapper (objectName 'ToolbarScroll') and that no QToolBar was added via addToolBar.
tests.expected_result: central min-hint width <= 750px, the toolbar is a descendant of the central widget, item 0 of the central layout is the scroll wrapper, and no QMainWindow toolbar area was used.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D19.4(ii): Given the toolbar is visible, Then every toolbar control remains reachable/usable — directly at a wide window and via the horizontal scroll/elide affordance at the narrowest window in which the dock minima plus chart minimum are feasible; the toolbar keeps its full natural width inside the scroll content so the horizontal scroll range is > 0 at a narrow width.
tests.description: At a narrow window width, assert the wrapper's horizontal QScrollBar maximum() > 0 (content wider than viewport) and every toolbar control (symbol_input, tf_combo, load_btn, mode_combo, studies_btn, alarms_btn, alarm_mode_btn, sound_btn, dom_btn, ext_hours_btn, tz_combo, draw_combo, draw_set_combo, draw_sets_btn, draw_delete_btn, conn_badge) is a descendant of the scroll content; at a wide window assert the controls lie within the viewport; assert the toolbar's laid-out height <= 40px.
tests.expected_result: Horizontal scroll range > 0 at the narrow width, all controls remain descendants of the scroll content, at the wide width the controls are directly visible, and the toolbar height is <= ~40px (one row).

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D19.5: Given the toolbar is visible, When the window is resized down toward the feasible minimum, Then centralWidget().width() decreases accordingly and does not remain at the toolbar's ~1716px minimum.
tests.description: Show the window at width 2400, then resize to 1200, processing events; assert centralWidget().width() is smaller at 1200 than at 2400 and is not pinned at ~1716 at the narrower width.
tests.expected_result: centralWidget().width() decreases with the window and does not remain at the toolbar's ~1716px minimum.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Structural/mechanism: Given the wrapped toolbar, Then the wrapper is a QScrollArea with frameShape NoFrame, setWidgetResizable(False), horizontal ScrollBarPolicy ScrollBarAsNeeded, vertical ScrollBarPolicy ScrollBarAlwaysOff and a fixed height of 36px; the toolbar carries objectName 'MainToolbar', the wrapper 'ToolbarScroll', and conn_badge and the trailing stretch stay inside the scroll region (FI-D19-2); the toolbar's control set and signal wiring are unchanged.
tests.description: Inspect the wrapper returned by findChild(QScrollArea, 'ToolbarScroll'): assert frameShape() == NoFrame, widgetResizable() is False, horizontalScrollBarPolicy() == ScrollBarAsNeeded, verticalScrollBarPolicy() == ScrollBarAlwaysOff, and its fixed height is 36; assert findChild(QWidget, 'MainToolbar') exists and conn_badge is a descendant of it (inside the scroll content).
tests.expected_result: All wrapper properties and objectNames match the D19 mechanism; conn_badge is inside the scroll region; no control construction or signal wiring changed.
